Guidance & outlook: Annual SIP inflows have compounded at more than 29% between FY21 and FY26, and full-year SIP contributions for FY26 came in at approximately ₹3.5 lakh crore, up close to 21% over the previous year.

Growth & demand: World output is estimated to have expanded by 3.4% in 2025, a number that masks a widening gap between advanced economies, which grew a moderate 1.9%, and emerging market and developing economies, which grew 4.4% on the back of continued strength in India and China.
World trade volumes grew a healthy 5.1%, a figure that would have been unremarkable in a calmer year but stood out in 2025 given how much tariff and trade-policy noise ran alongside it.

Brokerage revenue from this desk grew sharply in FY26, rising to ₹34,38,155 from ₹14,45,766 in FY25 - an increase of close to 138% - even as the broader broker - age line contracted, underscoring that institutional client en - gagement and market share gained ground through the year even as overall volumes were softer.
Margins & costs: Inflation eased through the year to average around 4.1% globally, helped by the lagged effects of earlier monetary tightening and better supply conditions.

On headline inflation, the government chose to absorb rather than pass through the shock when crude briefly crossed USD 100 per barrel in March 2026, cutting excise duty on petrol and diesel by ₹10 per litre rather than allowing pump prices to rise in line with crude a decision that kept consumer inflation contained even as the fiscal cost of the move added …

Mutual fund AUM crossed ₹73 lakh crore by March 2026, up more than 12% year-on- year, with passive fund AUM growing faster still, up over 22%, as cost-conscious and increasingly sophisticated investors continued to shift allocations toward index-based products alongside actively managed equity and hybrid schemes.
Capex & expansion: To support consumption, the government paired income-tax relief with a rationalisation of GST rates, while simultaneously protecting capital expenditure the FY2026-27 Budget allocated ₹12.2 lakh crore toward capex, signalling that growth-supportive spending was not being sacrificed for near-term consumption measures.

The active client base on the NSE has now grown to around 46 million, a 24% compounded annual growth rate from just 5.17 million a decade earlier in March 2016 - a pace of expansion that has held up through multiple market cycles, not just the buoyant ones.

Risks & challenges: RISK MANAGEMENT The Company has a risk management framework which not only ensures timely identification of risks, analysis of the reasons for such risk, assessment of its materiality, assessment of its impact but also adequate risk mitigation processes.

Against this backdrop, gold was the standout asset of the year, returning roughly 60%, while US Treasury yields stayed range-bound between 4% and 4.5%, closing near 4.31%, and the dollar carried a broadly weakening bias despite the volatility around it.

Economic Risk A broader slowdown in Indian economic growth, or sustained volatility in global commodity prices - particularly oil - could weigh on the Company's business, both directly through capital market activity and indirectly through the purchasing power and risk appetite of the Company's client base.
